title: Home 72-Hour Kit
description: Use this list to build the basic Ready.gov emergency kit that keeps your household going for the first 3 days without services.

sources.title: Be Prepared for a Power Outage

items.text: Water: at least 3 gallons (11 L) per person (1 gallon per person per day), more for hot weather, nursing mothers, sick people, and pets
3 days of non-perishable food your family will eat that needs little or no cooking
Manual can opener
Prescription medicines and a written list of medicines, doses, and allergies for each person
First aid kit
Flashlights with extra batteries (one per person) - not candles
Battery or hand-crank radio and a NOAA Weather Radio with alerts
Phone chargers and a charged backup battery
Battery-powered carbon monoxide alarm if you will use any fuel-burning device
Whistle to signal for help
Dust masks, plastic sheeting, scissors, and duct tape for sheltering in place
Wet wipes, garbage bags, and plastic ties for sanitation
Wrench or pliers to turn off utilities
Local paper maps
Glasses, contact lens supplies, hearing aid batteries, and other personal medical items
Infant formula, bottles, diapers, and wipes if you have a baby
Pet food, water, and supplies
Over-the-counter pain, fever, and stomach medicines (follow the label)
Soap, hand sanitizer, and feminine and personal hygiene items
Warm blanket or sleeping bag and a change of weather-appropriate clothes and sturdy shoes for each person
Fire extinguisher
Matches in a waterproof container
Cash in small bills and copies of key documents in a waterproof bag
Paper plates, cups, utensils, paper towels, and paper and pencil
Books, games, or puzzles for children
Pack it in 1-2 easy-to-carry bins or duffels in a cool, dry place everyone can reach, and check it once a year
